title: A Beginner’s Guide To British Politics (English Listening Practice)
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 哈喽，哈喽，哈喽，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上稀奇古怪又美妙的事情，同时提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about something that millions of people have strong opinions about, yet surprisingly few could explain clearly.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要讨论一个数百万人对此有强烈看法，然而出人意料地很少有人能清楚解释的话题。

sentences.en: British politics. We’ll talk about how the British political system works, where it comes from, why it looks the way it does, and some of the quirky features that make it very different to politics in other countries.
sentences.zh: 英国政治。我们将探讨英国政治体系是如何运作的、它的渊源是什么、为什么它会是现在的样子，以及一些使其与其他国家政治截然不同的独特色彩。

sentences.en: From how voting works to why this means British politics has historically been dominated by two parties, as well as where Scotland and Wales all fit in, I’m going to try to make it all make a little more sense.
sentences.zh: 从投票机制的运作方式到这意味着英国政治历史上为什么一直由两大政党主导，以及苏格兰和威尔士是如何融入其中的，我将努力让这一切变得更容易理解。

sentences.en: And perhaps oddly enough, in an episode about politics, I am going to make this as apolitical as possible, so this isn’t about saying one party is good and another is bad, but rather explaining how the entire system works.
sentences.zh: 也许听起来很奇怪，在一期关于政治的节目中，我将尽量保持客观中立，所以这不是为了说哪个政党好、哪个政党坏，而是为了解释整个系统是如何运作的。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们就废话少说，直接切入正题。

sentences.en: If you asked someone from outside the UK to describe British politics, you might hear something like this: “There’s a Prime Minister… and a King… and Lords…and something called Westminster… and people shouting at each other across an old room that looks far too small… and Scotland wants independence… and then there was Brexit…and there seems to be a new Prime Minister every five minutes.”
sentences.zh: 如果你问一个英国以外的人来描述英国政治，你可能会听到这样的话：“这里有一个首相……还有一个国王……还有贵族……还有个叫威斯敏斯特的地方……人们在一个看起来小得多的老房间里隔空对喊……苏格兰想要独立……然后还有英国脱欧……而且好像每隔五分钟就会换一个新首相。”

sentences.en: And to be fair, that’s not an entirely inaccurate summary.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，这个总结并不完全不准确。

sentences.en: British politics is unusual. It’s old, it’s full of quirky traditions, and it’s based far more on customs and conventions than on a single written rulebook.
sentences.zh: 英国政治很不寻常。它历史悠久，充满了奇特的传统，而且它更多地基于习俗和惯例，而不是一本单一的成文规则手册。

sentences.en: So over the next 20 minutes or so, I will try to explain how it works, so the next time you hear about an MP or the Commons or devolution, well, it might just be a little clearer.
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的20分钟左右里，我将尝试解释它是如何运作的，这样下次当你听到有关议员、下议院或权力下放的事情时，可能会更清楚一点。

sentences.en: The first thing to talk about is a little history, as there are two key events that shaped the modern political system.
sentences.zh: 我们要聊的第一件事是一点历史，因为有两个关键事件塑造了现代政治体系。

sentences.en: The first was all the way back in 1215, when the then King John I was forced by a group of powerful English barons to sign a document called the Magna Carta.
sentences.zh: 第一个要追溯到1215年，当时的国王约翰一世被一群强大的英国男爵逼迫签署了一份名为《大宪章》的文件。

sentences.en: What this did was establish the principle that the king [or queen] was not above the law, that the monarch couldn’t just do whatever they wanted.
sentences.zh: 这确立了一个原则，即国王（或女王）并非凌驾于法律之上，君主不能随心所欲。

sentences.en: I mean, they were still the most powerful person in the country, but it was the first time there were limits placed on this power.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们仍然是国内权力最大的人，但这是第一次对这种权力施加限制。

sentences.en: Fifty years later, in 1265, the first “semi-modern” parliament was called, when an English Earl called for representatives from counties, or districts, up and down the country, to come to the Palace of Westminster to discuss the management of the country.
sentences.zh: 五十年后的1265年，召开了第一届“半现代”议会，当时一位英国伯爵召集来自全国各郡或地区的代表来到威斯敏斯特宫，讨论国家管理问题。

sentences.en: And this, more than 760 years ago, was the basis for the political system that still exists today.
sentences.zh: 而这，在760多年前，就是今天仍然存在的政治体系的基础。

sentences.en: It has evolved significantly since then, with power shifting steadily from the monarch to Parliament, through civil wars, reforms, and revolutions.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，它发生了重大的演变，通过内战、改革和革命，权力稳步从君主转移到议会。

sentences.en: But today the country still has a monarch, there is still a parliament, which meets at Westminster, and is formed of representatives from up and down the country.
sentences.zh: 但今天国家仍然有君主，仍然有在威斯敏斯特开会的议会，并且由来自全国各地的代表组成。

sentences.en: So, let’s talk about Westminster, where it all began, and the tiny area of the country that is still, for better or for worse, the centre of British political power.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们来聊聊威斯敏斯特，一切开始的地方，以及至今无论好坏仍是英国政治权力中心的那一小块土地。

sentences.en: If you have been to London, you will probably have seen the British Parliament; it’s in the Palace of Westminster, beside the River Thames.
sentences.zh: 如果你去过伦敦，你可能已经见过英国议会了；它位于泰晤士河畔的威斯敏斯特宫。

sentences.en: It’s the big building with Big Ben, the clock tower, at one end.
sentences.zh: 这是一座在一端带有大本钟（钟楼）的大建筑。

sentences.en: Inside, parliament has two what's called chambers.
sentences.zh: 在内部，议会有两个所谓的议院。

sentences.en: The first is The House of Commons. And here “common” is short for commoner, just meaning a normal, non-titled or royal person.
sentences.zh: 第一个是下议院（House of Commons）。在这里，“Common”是平民的简称，仅指普通、无爵位或王室身份的人。

sentences.en: This is the heart of British politics, and where the 650 elected Members of Parliament, or MPs, sit.
sentences.zh: 这是英国政治的心脏，650名民选议员（MPs）就在这里开会。

sentences.en: The other chamber is called the House of Lords, which has around 800 members.
sentences.zh: 另一个议院被称为上议院（House of Lords），大约有800名成员。

sentences.en: Importantly, these Lords are not elected by the public; they can only be appointed by the monarch –the king or queen–but they are typically proposed by the Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，这些贵族不是由公众选举产生的，他们只能由君主（国王或女王）任命，但通常由首相提名。

sentences.en: Historically they were chosen because they were Lords, your father was a lord, so you would inherit his title after he died.
sentences.zh: 历史上，他们之所以被选是因为他们是贵族，你的父亲是贵族，所以你在他死后会继承他的头衔。

sentences.en: This, clearly, was not a very democratic system, so it was reformed, and the number of what’s called hereditary peers was greatly reduced.
sentences.zh: 很明显，这不是一个非常民主的体系，所以它进行了改革，被称为世袭贵族的数量大大减少。

sentences.en: Most members are now life peers, so people appointed for their expertise or their long public service, and importantly appointed for life; that’s why there isn’t a fixed number of them.
sentences.zh: 现在大多数成员都是终身贵族，也就是因其专业知识或长期公共服务而被任命的人，而且重要的是终身任命；这就是为什么他们的数量不是固定的。

sentences.en: They might be former politicians, scientists, lawyers, businesspeople, campaigners, or academics.
sentences.zh: 他们可能是前政客、科学家、律师、商界人士、活动家或学者。

sentences.en: Unlike hereditary peers, they cannot pass their title on to their children, and they usually serve until retirement or death.
sentences.zh: 与世袭贵族不同，他们不能将头衔传给子孙后代，他们通常任职到退休或去世。

sentences.en: So although the House of Lords still sounds aristocratic, and it’s clearly less democratic than the Commons, the modern version is more like a chamber of appointed specialists.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管上议院听起来仍然很贵族化，而且显然不如下议院民主，但现代版本更像是一个任命的专家院。

sentences.en: And the business of governing the country is split between these two houses: the House of Commons and the House of Lords.
sentences.zh: 治理国家的事务由这两个议院分担：下议院和上议院。

sentences.en: Typically the House of Commons will propose new laws, and it’s the House of Lords job to review and approve them.
sentences.zh: 通常下议院会提出新的法律，而审查和批准这些法律则是上议院的工作。

sentences.en: But crucially, it cannot block legislation indefinitely, forever.
sentences.zh: 但至关重要的是，它不能无限期地阻止立法。

sentences.en: If the elected House of Commons insists, its decision ultimately wins.
sentences.zh: 如果民选的下议院坚持，它的决定最终会获胜。

sentences.en: And then there is a third part of this political system, and that’s the monarch, the sitting king or queen.
sentences.zh: 然后是这个政治体系的第三部分，那就是君主，在位的国王或女王。

sentences.en: To an outsider, it might look like the monarch’s job is just to turn up in fancy clothes and a crown, and there is an element of truth to that.
sentences.zh: 对外行人来说，君主的工作似乎只是穿着华丽的衣服戴着王冠露面，这确实有一定的道理。

sentences.en: But the monarch still technically appoints the Prime Minister, opens Parliament, dissolves Parliament, meets the Prime Minister every week to discuss the state of the country, and gives the final say on any new laws.
sentences.zh: 但君主在技术上仍然任命首相、开闭议会、每周与首相会面讨论国家状况，并对任何新法律拥有最终决定权。

sentences.en: But, and this is an important but, the monarch will never go against Parliament.
sentences.zh: 但是，这是一个重要的“但是”，君主绝不会与议会作对。

sentences.en: To do so would be suicidal for the monarchy, and it has been more than three centuries since a British monarch went against an act of parliament.
sentences.zh: 这样做对君主制来说将是自杀式的，英国君主违背议会法案已经有三个多世纪没有发生了。

sentences.en: So it is essentially ceremonial, although officially the monarch could say no.
sentences.zh: 所以它本质上是象征性的，尽管官方上君主可以说不。

sentences.en: Supporters of this monarchical system argue that it provides stability, continuity, and a sense of national identity that’s above party politics.
sentences.zh: 这一君主制的支持者认为，它提供了超越党派政治的稳定感、延续性和国家认同感。

sentences.en: Critics say it's outdated and fundamentally undemocratic to have a king or queen that is in any way involved in the political system.
sentences.zh: 批评者则认为，拥有一个以任何方式参与政治体系的国王或女王是过时的，而且从根本上是不民主的。

sentences.en: Whatever your view, the practical reality is straightforward: The real political power in the UK lies with Parliament and the elected government, not with the crown.
sentences.zh: 无论你的观点如何，现实很简单：英国真正的政治权力在于议会和民选政府，而不是王冠。

sentences.en: The monarch is the constitutional figurehead, the symbolic centre of the system, but not the one making decisions.
sentences.zh: 君主是宪法上的名义领袖，是系统的象征中心，但不是决策者。

sentences.en: They reign but not rule, so the expression goes.
sentences.zh: 正如一句名言所说：他们统而不治。

sentences.en: So, who does rule? Well, the government.
sentences.zh: 那么，谁来统治呢？好吧，是政府。

sentences.en: And here, we must talk about how the British voting system works, how a party gains power, and how the Prime Minister is chosen.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们必须谈谈英国的投票系统是如何运作的，一个政党是如何获得权力的，以及首相是如何被选出的。

sentences.en: Unlike many democratic systems where citizens directly vote for the national leader, in the UK people do not vote for a Prime Minister, not directly at least.
sentences.zh: 与许多公民直接投票选举国家领导人的民主制度不同，在英国，人们不投票选举首相，至少不是直接投票。

sentences.en: The British Prime Minister as of the time of recording this episode is Keir Starmer, and in the 2024 national elections, he received a grand total of 18,884 votes.
sentences.zh: 在本集录制时，英国首相是基尔·斯塔默（Keir Starmer），在2024年的全国大选中，他总共获得了18884张选票。

sentences.en: You didn’t mishear that. 18,884. Now, you might be wondering how that’s possible.
sentences.zh: 你没有听错。18884张。现在，你可能在想这怎么可能。

sentences.en: A country of 70 million people, and the Prime Minister only received enough votes to fit a small football stadium.
sentences.zh: 一个拥有7000万人口的国家，首相获得的选票只够填满一个小型的足球场。

sentences.en: Well, the British voting system is different.
sentences.zh: 嗯，英国的投票系统与众不同。

sentences.en: The country is split into 650 areas, or constituencies as they are called.
sentences.zh: 全国被划分为650个区域，也就是所谓的选区（constituencies）。

sentences.en: These are divided broadly by the number of people in each area, so Greater London has 75, but the whole of Scotland only has 57.
sentences.zh: 这些选区大致根据每个区域的人口数量划分，因此大伦敦有75个，但整个苏格兰只有57个。

sentences.en: And at an election, British citizens registered in that constituency vote for candidates in that constituency, in that area.
sentences.zh: 在选举中，在该选区登记的英国公民为该选区内的候选人投票。

sentences.en: Typically each political party will propose one candidate per constituency, and the candidate who receives the most votes is elected the Member of Parliament for that constituency.
sentences.zh: 通常每个政党在每个选区推选一名候选人，获得最多票数的候选人当选该选区的国会议员。

sentences.en: So going back to Keir Starmer for a moment, he is the Labour MP for an area of London called Holborn and St Pancras.
sentences.zh: 所以回到基尔·斯塔默，他是伦敦一个叫霍尔本和圣潘克拉斯（Holborn and St Pancras）地区的工党议员。

sentences.en: That constituency only has around 75,000 registered voters, and he received just shy of 19,000 votes in the last election; he didn’t even receive a majority of votes in his own constituency.
sentences.zh: 该选区只有大约75000名注册选民，他在上次选举中只获得了不到19000张选票；他甚至没有在他自己的选区获得多数票。

sentences.en: So, you have 650 constituencies, each of which votes for its MP, and most MPs are part of a political party.
sentences.zh: 所以，你有650个选区，每个选区投票选出其议员，大多数议员都属于某个政党。

sentences.en: A party has a leader, and the leader of the party with the most MPs will become Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 一个政党有一位领袖，拥有最多议员的政党领袖将成为首相。

sentences.en: So in practice, yes, Keir Starmer might have only got fewer than 19,000 votes directly, but everyone voting for a Labour MP in their constituency was indirectly voting for him as Prime Minister, because he was the Labour leader.
sentences.zh: 所以在实践中，是的，基尔·斯塔默直接获得的选票可能不到19000张，但他们在选区投票给工党议员的每个人都在间接投票支持他担任首相，因为他是工党领袖。

sentences.en: The consequence of this system, the so-called “first past the post” system, is that it disproportionately rewards larger parties.
sentences.zh: 这个系统（即所谓的“多数代表制”或“得票最多者当选”系统）的结果是，它不成比例地奖励大党。

sentences.en: For example, if, theoretically, one large party wins 51% of the votes in every constituency, and the remaining 49% of the votes are split between two smaller parties, that large party would receive 100% of the MPs, and the smaller parties would receive 0%.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果从理论上讲，一个大党在每个选区都赢得了51%的选票，而剩下的49%的选票由两个小党瓜分，那么这个大党将获得100%的议席，而小党将获得0%。

sentences.en: And this advantage shows up in a few different ways.
sentences.zh: 这种优势体现在几个不同的方面。

sentences.en: First, millions of votes can end up making no difference at all.
sentences.zh: 首先，数百万张选票最终可能根本起不到任何作用。

sentences.en: A party whose support is spread thinly across the whole country might get a respectable share of the national vote but still fail to win a single parliamentary seat, simply because it never comes first in any constituency.
sentences.zh: 一个支持率薄弱分散在全国各地的政党可能会获得可观的全国得票份额，但仍然无法赢得哪怕一个议会席位，仅仅因为它在任何选区都没有获得第一名。

sentences.en: Second, the opposite can also be true: a party with support concentrated in one region can win a large number of seats with a relatively small share of the national vote.
sentences.zh: 其次，情况也可能正好相反：支持率集中在一个地区的一个政党可以凭借相对较小的全国得票份额赢得大量席位。

sentences.en: This is why regional parties—like the Scottish National Party—often do well under the First Past the Post system.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么像苏格兰民族党这样的地区政党往往能在“得票最多者当选”系统下表现良好。

sentences.en: Third, the system means that the national vote share and the number of MPs a party wins can look wildly out of proportion.
sentences.zh: 第三，这意味着全国得票率和一个政党赢得的议员数量可能会看起来极不对称。

sentences.en: A party might win a comfortable majority in Parliament with well under half of the popular vote, while another might win millions of votes and end up with almost no representation at all.
sentences.zh: 一个政党可能以远低于半数的普选票在议会中赢得舒适的多数席位，而另一个政党可能赢得数百万张选票，却几乎没有任何代表权。

sentences.en: This actually happened in the last election, in 2024.
sentences.zh: 这实际上在2024年的上一次大选中发生了。

sentences.en: The Labour Party won what was called a landslide victory, with 63% of the seats, but only won 34% of the popular vote.
sentences.zh: 工党赢得了所谓的压倒性胜利，获得了63%的席位，但普选得票率只有34%。

sentences.en: These are all variations of the same point: First Past the Post rewards parties that can win lots of constituencies, not necessarily lots of votes.
sentences.zh: 这些都是同一个观点的不同变体：“得票最多者当选”奖励那些能够赢得大量选区的政党，而不一定是赢得大量选票的政党。

sentences.en: Supporters say this delivers clear winners and stable governments; in the UK coalitions are quite rare, with only 19 of the past 100 years having a coalition in government.
sentences.zh: 支持者表示，这带来了清晰的赢家和稳定的政府；在英国，联合政府非常罕见，过去100年中只有19年是由联合政府执政的。

sentences.en: Critics, on the other hand, say it’s unfair and distorts the democratic will.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，批评者认为这很不公平，扭曲了民主意愿。

sentences.en: And this debate comes up at almost every election.
sentences.zh: 几乎每次选举都会引发这种辩论。

sentences.en: Whatever your opinion, First Past the Post is one of the defining features of British politics, and it shapes almost everything about how politicians campaign, governments are formed and how power changes hands.
sentences.zh: 无论你的观点如何，“得票最多者当选”是英国政治的决定性特征之一，它几乎塑造了政客如何竞选、政府如何组建以及权力如何交接的一切。

sentences.en: So, there is a national election–or general election–which typically happens every five years.
sentences.zh: 所以，会有一次全国大选（或大选），通常每五年举行一次。

sentences.en: British citizens vote for their regional MP, the results come in, and typically one political party will win a majority, more than 325, of the electoral seats.
sentences.zh: 英国公民投票选出他们的地区议员，结果出炉，通常一个政党会赢得多数席位（超过325个议席）。

sentences.en: Its leader will become Prime Minister, and he or she will appoint ministers to various positions of power.
sentences.zh: 它的领袖将成为首相，他或她将任命部长担任各个权力的职位。

sentences.en: Of course, this is politics, so they’ll choose this strategically based on alliances, rewarding supporters, punishing critics, and perhaps putting rivals in token positions of responsibility from where they cannot mount an attack.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是政治，所以他们会根据联盟、奖赏支持者、惩罚批评者，以及可能把竞争对手安排在没有实权但负有象征责任的职位上以防他们发起攻击，来战略性地做出选择。

sentences.en: But this certainly isn’t unique to British politics.
sentences.zh: 但这绝不是英国政治所独有的。

sentences.en: Now, let’s talk about what these MPs actually do.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们来谈谈这些议员实际上做什么。

sentences.en: Every MP, whether that is the Prime Minister, a government MP, or a member of a minor party, they are the elected representative of the people in their constituency.
sentences.zh: 每个议员，无论是首相、执政党议员还是小党成员，都是他们选区人民的民选代表。

sentences.en: This means that they have a duty to represent the interests and concerns of the people living in their area; they aren’t just representing their party or the country.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们有责任代表其生活在该地区的人民的利益和关切；他们不仅代表他们的政党或国家。

sentences.en: How this works in practice is that anyone can write to their MP about a concern they have, whether that’s something as weighty as government foreign policy or simply that the local post office is closing down.
sentences.zh: 这在实践中是如何运作的呢？任何人都可以就他们关心的某项问题写信给他们的议员，无论是像政府外交政策那样厚重的事情，还是仅仅是当地邮局要关门了。

sentences.en: And it’s the MP’s job to take these concerns to parliament, through some sort of filtering system, of course.
sentences.zh: 把这些关切带到议会去就是议员的工作，当然，这需要通过某种过滤系统。

sentences.en: And if you’ve seen clips of people standing up in an old-looking room with wooden benches with green fabric, shouting at each other, this is what’s happening.
sentences.zh: 如果你看过人们站在一个铺着绿色织物木质长椅、看起来很有年代感的房间里互相大喊大叫的片段，这就是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: The highlight of this is every Wednesday, at 12pm: Prime Minister’s Questions, or PMQs.
sentences.zh: 其中的重头戏是每周三中午12点：首相问答时间（PMQs）。

sentences.en: This is when MPs have the chance to ask the Prime Minister questions, questions that are typically intended to catch them out.
sentences.zh: 这是议员们有机会向首相提问的时候，这些问题通常旨在让他们难堪。

sentences.en: It’s here that you have the most heated debate, and this is all broadcast live, for anyone to see.
sentences.zh: 正是在这里，你会看到最激烈的辩论，而且这一切都是现场直播，供所有人观看。

sentences.en: It’s a fundamental part of the British political system, requiring the Prime Minister to respond to unscripted questions about his or her government’s performance every week that Parliament is open.
sentences.zh: 这是英国政治体系的一个基本部分，要求首相在议会开会的每一周都要就其政府的表现回答未经彩排的问题。

sentences.en: It certainly keeps the government on its toes.
sentences.zh: 这当然会让政府时刻保持警惕。

sentences.en: And this isn’t the only thing. The Prime Minister is only Prime Minister because he or she has the support of their party, the moment they lose that support is the moment they lose their job.
sentences.zh: 这还不是全部。首相之所以是首相，仅仅是因为他或她得到了党内的大力支持，一旦他们失去了这种支持，就是他们失去工作的时候。

sentences.en: This can happen in a couple of ways. Most commonly, it comes from inside their own party.
sentences.zh: 这可以通过几种方式发生。最常见的是来自他们自己党内的内部。

sentences.en: Political parties in the UK can remove their leader if enough of their MPs decide they no longer support them.
sentences.zh: 英国的政党如果觉得有足够多的议员不再支持他们，就可以罢免他们的党魁。

sentences.en: Different parties have different internal rules, but in practice it usually begins with a group of unhappy MPs writing to party authorities to demand a leadership contest.
sentences.zh: 不同的政党有不同的内部规则，但在实践中，通常是一群不满的议员写信给党内权威机构，要求举行领袖竞选。

sentences.en: If the leader loses that contest, they step down as party leader, and because the Prime Minister must be the leader of the governing party, they automatically stop being Prime Minister as well.
sentences.zh: 如果现任领袖在竞选中失利，他就会辞去党魁职务，而且由于首相必须是执政党领袖，他们也会自动不再担任首相。

sentences.en: Alternatively, a Prime Minister can lose support in the House of Commons itself.
sentences.zh: 或者，首相可能会失去下议院本身的支持。

sentences.en: The opposition can call what is known as a vote of no confidence, a formal test of whether the government still has the backing of a majority of MPs.
sentences.zh: 反对党可以发起所谓的“不信任投票”，这是一项正式测试，检验政府是否仍然拥有多数议员的支持。

sentences.en: If the government loses such a vote, convention says the Prime Minister must either resign or call a general election.
sentences.zh: 如果政府在这样的投票中失利，按惯例首相必须辞职或解散议会重新大选。

sentences.en: Both of these mechanisms — internal revolts within the governing party, or formal votes in Parliament — mean that a Prime Minister is never entirely secure.
sentences.zh: 这两种机制——执政党内部的叛变，或议会中的正式投票——意味着首相永远不会绝对安全。

sentences.en: They must constantly maintain the confidence of their colleagues and the support of the Commons.
sentences.zh: 他们必须时刻维持同僚的信任和下议院的支持。

sentences.en: And it’s this reliance on maintaining confidence that makes British politics so lively, for want of a better word.
sentences.zh: 正是这种对维持信任的依赖，使得英国政治如此生动，如果换个更好的词的话。

sentences.en: Governments that appear strong can unravel quickly, and Prime Ministers can go from untouchable to unemployed in a matter of days.
sentences.zh: 看似强大的政府可能会迅速瓦解，首相可以在几天内从不可触碰变成失业人员。

sentences.en: Or in the case of Liz Truss, who was Prime Minister back in 2022, she lasted a mere 44 days.
sentences.zh: 或者以丽兹·特拉斯（Liz Truss）为例，她在2022年担任首相时，仅坚持了44天。

sentences.en: Now, let’s move on and talk about the main political parties.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们继续谈谈主要的政党。

sentences.en: For much of the past 100 years, British politics has been dominated by two political parties: The Labour Party, which is currently in power, and the Conservative Party, which was in power for the last decade.
sentences.zh: 在过去的100年里，英国政治大体上由两个政党主导：目前当政的工党，以及在过去十年中执政的保守党。

sentences.en: No other party has had a majority since before the First World War.
sentences.zh: 自第一次世界大战之前以来，还没有其他政党获得过多数席位。

sentences.en: The Labour Party is traditionally centre-left, and is associated with workers’ rights, social equality, and public services.
sentences.zh: 工党传统上属于中左翼，与劳工权益、社会平等和公共服务联系在一起。

sentences.en: The Conservative party is centre-right, and is associated with free markets, limited government, and social conservatism.
sentences.zh: 保守党属于中右翼，与自由市场、有限政府和保守主义联系在一起。

sentences.en: For much of the 20th century, British politics was a back-and-forth contest between these two giants.
sentences.zh: 在整个20世纪的大部分时间里，英国政治一直是这两大巨头之间来回拉锯的竞争。

sentences.en: One would win an election and govern for a decade; then the other would return and reverse many of the policies, and depending on the mood at the time, both parties might shift slightly to the left or to the right.
sentences.zh: 一个党派赢得大选执政十年；然后另一个党派卷土重来，扭转了许多政策，根据当时的心情，两党可能会稍微向左或向右倾斜。

sentences.en: This created a political rhythm: Left, right, left, right.
sentences.zh: 这创造了一种政治节奏：左、右、左、右。

sentences.en: And this comes from the first past the post voting system that we talked about a few minutes ago.
sentences.zh: 这源于我们几分钟前讨论的“得票最多者当选”投票系统。

sentences.en: But it looks very possible that things might change.
sentences.zh: 但事情发生改变的可能性非常大。

sentences.en: The most popular political party according to current polls is not Labour or Conservatives, or even the historically small-but-sometimes-important Liberal Democrats; it’s a relatively new party called Reform.
sentences.zh: 根据目前的民调，最受欢迎的政党既不是工党，也不是保守党，甚至不是历史上规模虽小但有时很重要的自由民主党；而是一个相对较新的政党，名为改革党（Reform）。

sentences.en: Now, Reform was originally called the Brexit Party, a party which will, to quote its website directly, “stand up for British culture, identity and values.
sentences.zh: 现在，改革党最初被称为英国脱欧党，正如其网站上直接引用的那样，该党将“捍卫英国的文化、身份和价值观”。

sentences.en: Freeze immigration and stop the boats. Restore law and order.
sentences.zh: 冻结移民并制止偷渡船。恢复法律与秩序。

sentences.en: Repair our broken public services. Cut taxes to make work pay.
sentences.zh: 修复我们破碎的公共服务。减税使劳动有回报。

sentences.en: End government waste. Slash energy bills.
sentences.zh: 结束政府浪费。大幅削减能源账单。

sentences.en: Unlock real economic growth.” Its critics paint it as a far-right populist party, but its supporters say it is the only party capable of fixing a broken political system.
sentences.zh: 释放真正的经济增长。”它的批评者将其描绘为一个极右翼民粹主义政党，但其支持者表示，它是唯一能够修复破碎的政治体系的政党。

sentences.en: It certainly is increasingly popular, and the most recent opinion poll has it far ahead, with 27% vote share, to Labour’s 19% and The Conservatives 18%.
sentences.zh: 它肯定越来越受欢迎，最近的民意调查显示它远远领先，支持率达到27%，而工党为19%，保守党为18%。

sentences.en: The next general election is not scheduled to be held until 2029, so there is a long time for those numbers to move, and they most likely will have shifted by the time you listen to this.
sentences.zh: 下一次大选预计要到2029年才会举行，所以这些数字还有很长的时间变动，等你听到这里时，它们很可能已经发生了变化。

sentences.en: But if it continues this way, it may just be the first time in a century that the UK will not have a Labour or Conservative Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 但如果继续这样下去，这可能是一个世纪以来英国首次没有工党或保守党首相。

sentences.en: Now, there is one final thing to mention, and that is an additional complication to do with the unusual structure of the UK.
sentences.zh: 现在，还有最后一件事要提，那就是与英国不寻常结构相关的另一个复杂情况。

sentences.en: And this is something called devolution.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的权力下放（devolution）。

sentences.en: The United Kingdom is formed of four countries: England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 大不列颠及北爱尔兰联合王国由四个国家组成：英格兰、威尔士、苏格兰和北爱尔兰。

sentences.en: In response to growing calls for greater autonomy, especially in Scotland, starting in the late 1990s the UK started to transfer certain powers away from the central government to regional parliaments.
sentences.zh: 为了回应日益高涨的对更大自治权的呼声（特别是在苏格兰），从20世纪90年代末开始，英国开始将中央政府的一些权力移交给地区议会。

sentences.en: This means that there are regional parliaments in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 这意味着苏格兰、威尔士和北爱尔兰都有地区议会。

sentences.en: Each of these have slightly different powers to change laws, but they typically can pass laws on issues that affect that region, such as on education and health systems.
sentences.zh: 这些议会中的每一个都有略微不同的立法权力，但通常可以通过影响该地区的事务（如教育和卫生系统）的法律。

sentences.en: Interestingly enough, England, which is by far the largest part of the UK, has no devolved parliament of its own.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，作为英国迄今为止最大部分的英格兰，却没有自己的地方分权议会。

sentences.en: Its laws are made by Westminster. This creates a tension called the “West Lothian Question”.
sentences.zh: 它的法律是由威斯敏斯特制定的。这就产生了一个名为“西洛辛问题”（West Lothian Question）的紧张局势。

sentences.en: Scottish MPs can vote on laws that only affect England, such as English schools or hospitals.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰议员可以对只影响英格兰的法律（如英格兰的学校或医院）进行投票。

sentences.en: But English MPs cannot vote on similar laws for Scotland, because Scotland controls those matters itself.
sentences.zh: 但英格兰议员不能对苏格兰的类似法律投票，因为苏格兰自己控制这些事务。

sentences.en: It's a small but important question. So, to wrap things up, the British political system is not perfect.
sentences.zh: 这是一个小但很重要的问题。所以，总而言之，英国的政治体系并不完美。

sentences.en: It's a patchwork of rituals, culture, and history.
sentences.zh: 它是由仪式、文化和历史拼凑而成的。

sentences.en: But at its core there are some important principles: nobody is above the law, Members of Parliament exist to serve the people, and there are checks and balances to ensure that anyone not doing a good job is swiftly sacked.
sentences.zh: 但其核心有一些重要原则：没有人能凌驾于法律之上，国会议员的存在是为了服务人民，并且有制衡机制以确保任何干不好工作的人会被迅速解雇。

sentences.en: It is imperfect, but to quote the two-time British Prime Minister, Winston Churchill, “Many forms of Government have been tried, and will be tried in this world of sin and woe.
sentences.zh: 它并不完美，但正如两任英国首相温斯顿·邱吉尔所说：“在这个充满罪恶和悲伤的世界里，人们已经尝试过并且将继续尝试各种形式的政府。

sentences.en: No one pretends that democracy is perfect or all-wise.
sentences.zh: 没有人声称民主是完美的或全知的。

sentences.en: Indeed it has been said that democracy is the worst form of Government except for all those other forms that have been tried from time to time.”
sentences.zh: 事实上，有人说过，除了历史上不时尝试过的所有其他形式的政府之外，民主是最糟糕的政府形式。”

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on the weird and wacky, and sometimes wonderful, world of British politics.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的节目就到这里，我们探讨了英国政治这个古怪、滑稽有时又美妙的世界。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这个节目很有趣，并且你学到了新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对这一集的看法。

sentences.en: What was surprising to you about British politics?
sentences.zh: 关于英国政治，什么让你感到惊讶？

sentences.en: If you live in the UK, what do you think will happen in the next election?
sentences.zh: 如果你住在英国，你认为下一次大选会发生什么？

sentences.en: And how does the political system in the UK differ from that in your country?
sentences.zh: 英国的政治体系与你国家的政治体系有何不同？

sentences.en: I would love to know, so let’s get this discussion started.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道，所以让我们开始讨论吧。

sentences.en: Let me know in the comments below, if you're listening to this somewhere where you can comment, and for the members among you, you can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 如果你在可以评论的地方收听这个节目，请在下方的评论区告诉我；对于我们当中的会员，你可以直接进入我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他好奇的心灵畅聊吧。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你一直在收听由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目再见。
